spec.question: for every published additive-vs-compounded pair in the E183-E190 delta family, is the printed sign a direction or a rounding-scale artefact?
spec.method: walk every results/*.json, take every dict carrying both an additive level and a compounded gap, publish |level|/|gap| and classify against two floors declared before the sweep was read

classes.sign_is_hair: |level| < ratio_floor*|gap| -- the printed sign must not be quoted
classes.level_agrees: |gap| < gap_floor_bp -- no gap to speak of, no sign question
classes.sign_quotable: |level| >= ratio_floor*|gap| -- the additive reading is big enough to be told apart from the gap

spec.answer_blind: the classification uses only the two published numbers; no threshold was moved after a cell was seen

honest: the two floors are declared constants, not fitted: 5% of the gap and 1bp of gap
a cell prints both numbers but the face never says which one a reader should quote
gap_needed_for_quotable_bp is what the gap would have to be for this same level to carry a quotable sign at the declared floor -- a scale statement, not a forecast
cells outside the E183-E190 family are included only if they publish both numbers
law_ref: O-20260924-1626 R3 (advisory: reader-facing defect, zero-bp cost)
